diagnosis.summary: product-service has been degraded for 4 minutes, with p95 end-to-end latency spiking from 6 ms to 1586 ms, a 264x increase. A 5xx error rate of 0.4% has appeared where none existed before. Request rate is essentially flat at 15.1 rps against a baseline of 15.0 rps.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB read throttling on the product-service table is the most likely root cause, with read capacity consumption rising 24.8x and 1400 read throttle events per minute where there were none at baseline.
evidence: p95 end-to-end latency rose from 6 ms to 1586 ms, a 264x increase, while p50 latency stayed nearly flat at 6 ms versus a baseline of 5 ms, indicating the degradation is confined to the tail of the distribution.
p95 DynamoDB call latency rose from 4 ms to 1580 ms, a 395x increase, closely tracking the overall p95 latency spike.
Read throttle events rose from 0 to 1400 per minute, indicating active throttling on the product-service DynamoDB table.
DynamoDB consumed read capacity rose from 480 RCU/min to 11900 RCU/min, a 24.8x increase.
The 5xx error rate is now 0.4% (0.004) against a baseline of 0.0, reflecting a small share of requests failing outright.
Request rate is flat at 15.1 rps versus a baseline of 15.0 rps, showing no traffic surge accompanying the read capacity increase.
recommended_actions: Increase provisioned read capacity units on the product-service DynamoDB table, or enable on-demand capacity mode, to absorb the current 11900 RCU/min consumption.
Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) or add application-level caching in the product-service Lambda to reduce repeated reads hitting the table.

Inspect the product-service Lambda handler for any recently introduced scan operations or missing key conditions that could explain the 24.8x increase in read capacity consumption without a traffic change.
Review DynamoDB CloudWatch metrics for hot partition indicators on the product-service table, which can cause localized throttling even when aggregate capacity appears sufficient.
Set a CloudWatch alarm on read_throttle_events for the product-service table so future throttling is detected before it reaches p95 latency impact.
